summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere. He was an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and later joined the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his BA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He served as a professor at Middlebury College and became a distinguished university professor at the University of Michigan.
Dondub Buddhayin was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who taught Eugène Obermiller. He served as abbot of Ganden Dargye Ling and Chilttai Monastery.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye. He also taught both Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, as well as Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy and abbot of Dinghui Monastery, later founding the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Culture.

Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeologist and historian who earned degrees from the University of Cincinnati, Yale, and Oxford (DPhil 1965–1968). From circa 1970 to 2011, she held posts at the University of Oxford and the Classical Art Research Centre.

Donna Lynn Brown specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees from the University of Manitoba and Maitripa College. She worked for the Government of Canada (1985–2011) and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Manitoba in 2023.
Donna Strahan is a specialist in history and archaeology. She served as a conservator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art and was appointed Head at the National Museum of Asian Art in 2014.
Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He served as a professor at Tribhuvan University from circa 1975 to 1993 and founded the Karnali Institute.
Doranne Jacobson is an anthropologist working in Indology who earned her doctorate from Columbia University. She has served as a seminar associate at Columbia University's Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is an Indologist and historian of religion who earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. She served as a curator at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art and as a research professor at Stony Brook University.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was a Tibetan Buddhist figure who studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, and several other masters. He was also a teacher of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dorje Tseten (1925–2013) was a Tibetologist and historian who earned an education degree from Beijing Normal University around 1944–1948. He served as the director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Kazan State University between 1842 and 1846 under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

Dorji Penjore is a researcher in Tibetology and history who completed a PhD in anthropology at the Australian National University. He was chief researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH and later became head/assistant professor at the Royal Institute of Management.

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. He began teaching there in 1998, becoming a professor in 2009.

Dorothy C. Wong specializes in Buddhist studies and art history/archaeology, holding degrees from International Christian University, CUHK, and Harvard University (PhD 1995). She has served on the faculty at the University of Virginia and as a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong.
